text: Cuts and scrapes are a part of childhood.

In most cases, they're not serious
and can be treated at home.

If the wound is bleeding,
press sterile gauze or a clean

cloth firmly on it until
the bleeding stops.

Hold the area under cool,
gentle running water.

You can also use bottled
water or saline wound spray.

Remove any debris by rubbing gently 
with a clean cloth or use clean tweezers.

Don't apply any disinfecting
solutions to the wound.
They don't help and will only cause pain.

Use a bandage to cover the
wound until a scab has formed.

Change the dressing every day or
more often if it gets wet or dirty.

Once a cut or scrape has formed a 
scab, you can leave it open to the air.
